episode.title: Recover from premature stream closure through the existing network-retry path
episode.before: At parent e80d7cc08303c78813508a9ea028f06fd3121e06, the retry classifier's exact network-code allowlist did not contain ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE. Consequently, a streamed response that yielded partial content and then failed with that code was not recognized by this code-based transient-network-error predicate.
episode.after: At f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba, ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE is an admitted retryable network code. The streaming retry test demonstrates the intended behavior: after an initial stream yields incomplete content and throws that error, the chat emits a retry event, obtains and emits a completed response from a subsequent stream attempt, and records the concrete error code in retry telemetry.
episode.diff: The implementation adds one exact error code to the shared retryable-network-code allowlist in packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts. A 62-line regression test in packages/core/src/core/geminiChat_network_retry.test.ts constructs a mid-stream premature-close failure followed by a successful stream and asserts retry signaling, successful replacement output, and error-type telemetry. No retry limits, delays, abort behavior, or generic error matching were changed.

evidence_units.claim: Commit f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba has parent e80d7cc08303c78813508a9ea028f06fd3121e06 and subject "fix(core): retry on ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE errors (#26519)".
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba; git rev-parse f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba^

evidence_units.claim: The implementation change adds the exact string ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE to RETRYABLE_NETWORK_CODES and makes no other production-code modification.

The shared retry predicate extracts an error code, tests it against the retryable network-code allowlist or the SSL pattern, and returns true when it matches; retry telemetry uses the same classification path to return the concrete code.
evidence_units.source: git show f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba:packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts (RETRYABLE_NETWORK_CODES, isRetryableSslErrorCode, getNetworkErrorCode, getRetryErrorType, and isRetryableError)

evidence_units.claim: In the parent implementation, RETRYABLE_NETWORK_CODES ends with UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT and does not include ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE.

The regression exercises the user-visible streaming call site by invoking GeminiChat.sendMessageStream and consuming its asynchronous event stream after enabling configured fetch-error retry behavior.
evidence_units.source: git show f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba:packages/core/src/core/geminiChat_network_retry.test.ts (test "should retry on premature stream closure (ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE)")

evidence_units.claim: The new test's first generated stream yields an incomplete chunk and then throws an Error whose code is ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE; the second generated stream yields a completed response with finishReason STOP.
The regression oracle requires a RETRY stream event, a CHUNK containing "Complete response after retry", and a network-retry telemetry call whose error_type is ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE.
evidence_units.source: git show f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba:packages/core/src/core/geminiChat_network_retry.test.ts (assertions in the premature stream closure test)

candidate_atomics.name: classify-premature-stream-closure-as-retryable
candidate_atomics.title: Classify premature stream closure as a transient network failure
candidate_atomics.description: Admit a specific premature-stream-termination code to an existing bounded network-error retry policy so interrupted streaming requests can use the established retry and telemetry path.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a streamed operation interrupted by a recognized premature-close transport error to recover through the existing retry mechanism instead of terminating immediately.
semantic_action.module_role: Shared transient-network-failure classifier used by retry execution and retry telemetry
semantic_action.pre_state: A streaming attempt has failed with an error carrying code ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE, but that code is absent from the exact retryable network-code set.
semantic_action.post_state: The existing network-error predicate recognizes ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE as retryable, and retry telemetry preserves that code as the failure type.
semantic_action.validation: Simulate a stream that emits partial content and throws the coded error, then provide a successful subsequent stream; require a retry event, completed response content, and telemetry labeled with the exact error code.

candidate_workflows.name: recover-recognized-premature-stream-termination
candidate_workflows.title: Recover a streamed operation after a recognized premature transport close
candidate_workflows.description: Extend an existing bounded network-retry policy with a narrowly identified premature-close code, then validate recovery at the streaming boundary, including retry signaling, completed output, and failure classification telemetry.

workflow_graph.goal: Convert a reproducible, coded premature stream closure from an immediate terminal failure into a bounded retry that can deliver a complete subsequent response while retaining observable retry diagnostics.
when_to_use: A streaming API can yield partial data and then fail with a stable transport error code that is known to represent premature connection closure.
An existing retry framework already classifies transient network codes and wraps or governs stream recovery.
A regression can reproduce failure during stream iteration and supply a successful later attempt.
anti_goals: Do not make every stream exception retryable.
Do not alter retry counts, backoff timing, jitter, abort handling, or quota/server-status policies when only one transport classification is missing.
Do not treat the partial response from the failed attempt as proof of successful completion.
Do not suppress the concrete failure type from retry telemetry.
not_applicable_when: The failure has no stable evidence that it is transient or safe to retry.
The operation is non-replayable or retrying could duplicate externally visible side effects.
Cancellation or abort requested by the caller caused the stream termination.
The retry framework does not cover failures raised during stream iteration.
The task requires changing retry exhaustion, delay, or response-reconciliation semantics rather than admitting a missing error classification.
inputs: A reproducible mid-stream failure and its concrete error object/code
The existing transient-network-error classifier and retry policy
A successful subsequent-stream fixture or equivalent integration oracle
workflow_graph.entry_state: A stream may emit incomplete content and then terminate with ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE; the shared exact-code classifier does not recognize that code, so the established recovery path cannot select it for retry.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The premature-close code is narrowly classified as retryable, and a streaming regression proves that the failure produces a retry signal, a complete response from the next attempt, and telemetry containing the concrete error type.

steps.condition: Apply only after reproducing a stream-iteration failure carrying the stable premature-close transport code and confirming the operation is covered by the existing bounded retry path.
steps.validation: The regression stream first yields incomplete content and throws ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE, then the consumed event stream contains RETRY and the completed second-attempt chunk; retry telemetry reports error_type ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: verify the exact transport code is added to the bounded retryable-code set without broadening generic exception matching.
Classifier-path check: verify code extraction feeds both retry eligibility and retry error-type reporting.
Streaming regression: fail after a partial chunk, then require an explicit retry event and completed output from the subsequent stream.
Observability check: require retry telemetry to retain the exact premature-close code.
Broader automated test or CI execution is desirable but is not established by the available evidence bundle.
stop_conditions: Stop if the observed error code differs from the proposed exact classification and no equivalence is established.
Stop if replaying the streaming operation is not safe.
Stop if the failure is an explicit abort or cancellation.
Stop if the stream layer cannot route iteration-time failures through the existing retry mechanism.
Stop after bounded retries are exhausted; this change does not authorize infinite retrying.
unresolved_or_deferred: Dynamic test execution and CI status are not available in the inspected evidence.
Issue/PR body, discussion, review rationale, and status-check metadata are unavailable, so the safety rationale is inferred only from implementation and regression-test behavior.
Behavior after retry exhaustion and reconciliation of already-emitted partial chunks are unchanged by this commit and are outside the extracted action.

unresolved_questions: Was the new regression and the broader core test suite executed successfully in CI? The bundle explicitly lacks status-check metadata, and no dynamic execution result was available.
What production runtime or dependency first surfaced ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE? The unavailable issue/PR discussion prevents attributing a more specific origin.

Does the consumer discard, display, or otherwise reconcile partial chunks emitted before the retry event? The commit tests recovery and final successful output but does not change or fully specify partial-output reconciliation.
